transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-18
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jordan Miles (Catalyst VP Eng), Rosa Park (Catalyst SRE), Evan Cho (Catalyst CTO)

Summary (auto): POC to validate unit economics for chat+generation workload. Goal is to determine hosted vs dedicated threshold, expected per-token cost with batching/caching, success criteria and timeline for a 6-week POC.

00:00 Alex Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, im Alex from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account, and with me is Priya our SE. quick note, audio is a little echoey?
00:12 Jordan Miles: yeah a little but it's fine. thanks for doing this. the main ask is we want a POC to show predictable cost for our customer-facing chat assistant, plus headroom for peak traffic.
00:25 Priya Nair: great, can you give a quick outline of the workload? avg tokens per session, concurrency, tail latencies you care about?
00:35 Jordan Miles: sure — typical session 150 to 400 tokens, prompts range 30 to 120 tokens plus generation 100 to 300 tokens, average about 220 tokens per request. concurrency during business hours ~120 qps sustained, with spikes to ~400 for 60-90s.
00:55 Rosa Park: also note we have strict data retention rules, logs older than 30 days go to cold storage and we need SOC2 and SAML SSO for any hosted vendor.
01:05 Priya Nair: okay that helps. rough success criteria? what would you consider success for the POC?
01:10 Evan Cho: primary is per-conversation cost under $0.02 for the 220 token average at p95 latency under 350ms. secondary is no PII leakage in logs and ability to pin model versions for rollouts.
01:25 Alex Chen: good concrete targets. on per-token economics we typically break down cost into compute per-token + inferred infra overhead + amortized caching gains. for hosted we can estimate per-token runtime compute; for Dedicated you get better predictability but you are paying reserved capacity.
01:42 Priya Nair: to give numbers, if you use a 7B-13B open model quantized to int8 on our hosted path with batching and prefix KV caching we typically see per-output-token GPU time of ~0.9-1.2 ms on an A100-class instance equivalent — translates to about $0.00002 to $0.00003 per token compute at current cloud GPU spot rates; network and infra bump that to around $0.000025-$0.00004 when averaged across workload.
02:10 Jordan Miles: wait can you repeat that? those decimals are easy to mess up, my finance person will freak if we undercount.
02:16 Priya Nair: yeah, so compute-only per-token for that model family in quantized mode is roughly 2.5 to 3 cents per 1,000 tokens, or $0.000025 to $0.00003 per token. with batching and prefix caching we reduce effective tokens served by up to 15-40% depending on prompt overlap — so your observed per-customer cost could drop to around $0.000018 per token in best-case.
02:45 Rosa Park: how sensitive is that to batch size? we cant introduce too much batching delay.
02:50 Priya Nair: batching is a latency-cost tradeoff. in continuous batching we set a max latency SLO, e.g., 50ms, 100ms. if you allow 50ms queueing you get smaller batches than 100ms, and cost savings shrink. For your p95 350ms SLO, you can safely allow 60-80ms batching windows and still be mid-200s latency. That typically yields batching factor of 1.6-2.3 for our workload distribution.
03:25 Evan Cho: ok and caching? how do we estimate prefix hit rates? we have a lot of templated prompts and user profile prefixes.
03:31 Priya Nair: prefix/KV caching depends on repetition. from similar customers with templated flows we saw hit rates 12-28% on prefix caches. with additional client-side prompt dedupe you can push that higher. in model terms a 20% prefix hit reduces billed generation tokens by 20% roughly, so it's a big lever.
03:50 Jordan Miles: good. on the hosted pricing side, can you give baseline per-month cost at our expected load (220 tokens avg, 120 qps sustained)?
03:59 Priya Nair: quick calc: 120 qps * 3600 * 24 * 30 = ~311 million requests per month? wait that's wrong, that's per-second, multiply by tokens; we should do this step by step.
04:12 Alex Chen: i'll simplify: 120 qps sustained * average 220 tokens * 3600 * 24 * 30 = approx 68.6 billion tokens/month. at $0.00003 per token compute baseline that's about $2.06M; that seems off — you're right it's big, let's re-check traffic units.
04:35 Jordan Miles: that is definitely too high, we meant 120 concurrent sessions with average 0.2 requests per second per session — I should've clarified, sorry.
04:45 Priya Nair: okay if it's 120 concurrent users with 0.2 rps that's 24 rps sustained. 24 rps * 220 tokens * 3600 * 24 * 30 = ~13.6 billion tokens/month. at $0.00003 that's ~408k/month compute. with batching/caching savings and multi-model routing maybe 25% reduction => ~306k/month.
05:15 Rosa Park: that monthly figure is still high for our budget, we have an initial POC budget of $40k for 6 weeks.
05:22 Alex Chen: that's normal, and the POC will be scoped smaller: for the POC we'll run a targeted benchmark simulating peak 1-hour window and typical day-to-day for 2 weeks, not full production traffic. we'll provide detailed per-scenario cost projections.
05:36 Jordan Miles: ok what about Dedicated — how does reserved capacity change the arithmetic?
05:40 Priya Nair: Dedicated reduces unit cost if you reach commit levels. For example a dedicated GPU pool with reserved nodes could cut compute cost per token by ~25-40% depending on utilization and model choice. But you pay the reserved monthly fee. For short-term POC you likely start hosted to validate correctness and then run a capacity sizing exercise for Dedicated.
06:02 Evan Cho: can Redwood support hybrid routing? like hosted for baseline and fall back to Dedicated or lower-capacity models during peaks?
06:09 Alex Chen: yes, smart routing is a core pattern — policy-based routing by latency, cost, or region. we can set a fallback model that's smaller or quantized when capacity is constrained to keep tail SLOs.
06:22 Jordan Miles: important question — we need audit logs, KMS integration and ability to control retention. can you meet SOC2 requirements?
06:30 Alex Chen: yes we have SOC2 and offer per-customer audit logs, SAML SSO, and KMS/HSM integrations for Private deployments. we'll attach the security pack.
06:38 Rosa Park: for the POC we still want to see logs but masked and stored for 14 days only. is that doable?
06:44 Priya Nair: yes we can set retention rules and mask tokens as part of the ingest path; we'll include that in the POC config.
06:52 Jordan Miles: great. what's the benchmark plan look like? we need perf numbers (p50/p95 latency), cost per 1k tokens under different batching windows, and stability under a 10-minute spike to 400 qps equivalent.
07:05 Priya Nair: plan is: 1) run baseline single-instance run of sample prompt set to capture per-token latencies; 2) run distributed load sim at your traces for 2x and 4x scale to observe batching, tail latency and failure modes; 3) run caching-enabled vs caching-disabled runs to estimate hit rates; 4) run quantization variants (fp16 vs int8) to measure quality/perf tradeoff. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens for each run.
07:36 Alex Chen: we'll also run an A/B of model variants — a 7B quantized small model vs a 13B quantized to see cost/latency/QA.
07:45 Jordan Miles: how long until we get results?
07:48 Priya Nair: we can provision test infra and run the baseline within 5 business days after we get your anonymized traces and sample prompts. full benchmark set — about 10 business days. so about 2 weeks end-to-end.
08:00 Jordan Miles: timeline fits. POC duration? we're expecting 6 weeks including integration, benchmarks and handoff.
08:07 Alex Chen: yes typical POC is 4-6 weeks; we can compress if you want. cost to Redwood for a POC is typically covered by usage on hosted plus a small services fee if you want assistance from SEs.
08:20 Rosa Park: for approvals we need a simple spreadsheet with line items we can present to finance — monthlyized estimates, sensitivity to batching and caching, Dedicated break-even point.
08:30 Alex Chen: I'll send that spreadsheet. it will include low/expected/high usage scenarios, pre/post cache, and dedicated commit vs hosted comparisons with break-even months.
08:40 Evan Cho: one more — we need an SLA if we move to Dedicated. what uptime do you offer and how is latency SLO measured?
08:48 Alex Chen: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. latency SLO is measured at the model-route level (p95) and we provide tracing hooks and dashboards in Redwood Console. we'll include sample SLA language.
08:58 Jordan Miles: ok this was helpful. can you summarize the immediate deliverables?
09:02 Alex Chen: sure — 1) Cost model spreadsheet (Alex) due 6/20; 2) Benchmark test plan + sample prompts (Priya) due 6/22; 3) Customer to share anonymized traces (Rosa) due 6/23; 4) Schedule SE deep-dive week of 6/29.
09:18 Jordan Miles: perfect. we'll reconvene after we get the spreadsheet. thanks everyone.
09:25 Meeting end.
